key_idea: A complete edge-coloured graph with no properly coloured cycle always has a vertex whose edges to all remaining vertices share one colour; peeling such vertices gives an order v1..vn with colour c_i from v_i to everything later. Then f(S) = 1 + (max multiplicity of a colour among the non-last vertices of S).
sketch: Repeatedly find and remove a vertex whose edges to all still-alive vertices are monochromatic (O(n^3) total), recording its colour. A monochromatic clique inside S is some colour-c vertices plus one final vertex later in the order, so with u the last vertex of S, f(S) = 1 + max_c cnt_c(S minus u). For each prefix length p, sum over subsets of the first p vertices of the max colour count via sum over t of (2^p - prod_c sum_{j<=t} C(a_c, j)), using prefix sums of binomials. Total work about n^3/12 multiplications. Pitfalls: the last vertex in the order has no colour (acts as a wildcard), and everything is mod 1e9+7. Verified against a brute force over all valid colourings of up to 6 vertices.
